**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** Leaf
- **Key features:**
  - Large, roughly oval/elliptical lesion on an otherwise green banana leaf
  - The lesion has a **dark brown to black necrotic center**
  - Surrounded by a distinct **yellowish-orange halo** transitioning outward from the dark core
  - The lesion appears isolated — a single, well-defined spot
  - Background leaf tissue is uniformly dark green

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Anthracnose:** Typically affects fruit/post-harvest; small water-soaked spots
- **Bunchy_Top:** Virus causing stunted growth, dark green streaks on leaves — no lesions
- **Cigar_End_Rot:** Affects the tip of banana fruit, not leaves
- **Cordana Leaf Spot:** Causes oval/elliptical spots with brown center and yellow halo — closely matches, but typically has a lighter tan/brown center
- **Panama Disease:** Causes yellowing and wilting of whole leaves/plant, vascular discoloration — not isolated leaf spots
- **Yellow and Black Sigatoka:** Causes streaks that develop into spots with **dark brown/black centers** and **yellow halos** — this matches very well. The characteristic dark necrotic center with a prominent yellow-orange border is the hallmark of Sigatoka complex diseases

The lesion — a single large oval spot with a **jet-black necrotic center** and **bright yellow-orange halo** on a green leaf — is most consistent with **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka** (Black Sigatoka / *Mycosphaerella fijiensis*), which produces exactly this type of dark, circular lesion with a yellow border on banana leaves.

This pattern — dark necrotic core with yellow border on a green leaf — is the hallmark symptom of Yellow and Black Sigatoka (Black Sigatoka, caused by Mycosphaerella fijiensis), distinguishing it from Cordana Leaf Spot (lighter tan centers) and Panama Disease (systemic yellowing/wilting rather than discrete leaf spots)."}
